## General Circular to Licensed REIT Managers Frequently Asked Question on disclosure of distribution composition

The SFC has recently updated the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) relating to real estate investment trusts (REITs) on its website.

We would like to draw your attention to one of the new FAQs, which elaborates on the ongoing operational requirements in respect of the disclosure of distributions declared or made by REITs.  This FAQ is set out below for your ease of reference:

'What are the disclosure requirements in respect of the composition of distribution made by a REIT?

In order to enhance transparency and investors' understanding of the composition of distributions  declared  by  REITs,  all  REITs  must  disclose  clearly  (a)  the  extent  to which the distribution declared or made by it is composed of, and the types of, income and capital and (b) any amounts deducted (such as taxes in respect of distributions paid/payable  to  unitholders)  pursuant  to  its  trust  deed,  in  all  of  their  results announcements, semi-annual and annual reports.  For example, any adjustment made to the distribution amount as a result of the adding back of the amortisation charge of the  upfront  swap  payment  to  distributable  income  will  normally  be  regarded  as  an effective return of capital for this purpose, and the SFC would require disclosure of such  amount  on  a  per  unit  basis  as  a  minimum.    Managers  should  consult  the Investment Products Department if they have any query as to the extent of disclosure required.'

The  full version of the updated FAQs  can  be  found  on  the SFC's  website under 'Intermediaries, Licensing and Investment Products - Investment Products Related Matters FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions Relating to Real Estate Investment Trusts'.

If you wish to clarify any aspects of the requirements set out in the FAQ, please contact the relevant team supervisor or case officer of the Investment Products Department.
